topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the complement system and contextualizes its importance and complexity in immunology.

topics.label: Fundamentals and core concepts of the complement system
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the foundational organizational principles and molecular mechanisms that govern the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three biochemical pathways that recognize targets and drive activation toward the threshold of C3 convertase deposition.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the functional downstream processes through which activated complement eliminates pathogens and stimulates immune activity.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the cellular and soluble regulatory mechanisms that prevent complement from damaging healthy host tissues.

topics.label: Clinical complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how deficiencies across individual complement components manifest in specific clinical diseases and pathologies.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the molecular strategies evolved by microorganisms to circumvent complement defenses and how these mechanisms are applied in the laboratory.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer wraps up the lecture on complement and previews the upcoming lecture on the adaptive immune system.
